about: Platinum Road's recommended route to the GTA VI platinum, in four phases. The phases are a recommended order, not a lockout order: almost everything in the game stays available after the story ends. The one hard exception is trophy 28, Positive Mental Attitude — one of its meditation spots disappears when Chapter 1 ends, which is why it sits in Phase 2 even though the rest of the collectibles could wait.
difficultyNotes: Estimated difficulty 5/10 and roughly 90–100 hours: a 60–80 hour story campaign, then a long but checklist-driven 100% grind and a short cleanup. Nothing is tied to online play or DLC. Only one trophy (id 28) is missable. Methods for trophies 44, 45, 49, 50 and 51 were unconfirmed in every source checked at the time of writing, so this roadmap routes them with the other miscellaneous trophies and flags them in the checklist instead of printing steps nobody has verified.

phases.goal: Play the five-chapter campaign (about 60–80 hours) and bank the 19 automatic story trophies as they come. Build platinum-friendly habits from the start: scan every new vehicle you enter and study new animals whenever you travel, because that progress feeds the 100% completion trophy later.
phases.name: Story first

phases.goal: Grab what the story can take away, in the order it becomes available. Trophy 28 is the priority: one of its meditation spots is tied to a Chapter 1 invitation at Jason's house and is gone for good once the chapter ends. Pick up the other collectibles as their areas open up so Phase 3 starts with most of them already banked.
phases.name: Grab it during the story

phases.goal: With the story done, the in-game 100% checklist (Progress > Stats) becomes the guide: work through the remaining side jobs, collectibles and activities, plus the miscellaneous one-off trophies. The platinum itself (id 1) unlocks automatically once the other 54 are earned.
phases.name: The 100% grind

phases.goal: Finish the slow accumulators and skill-based leftovers (about 10–20 hours). These six trophies reward repetition and technique rather than exploration, so they are the natural final sweep once everything else is done.
phases.name: Cleanup
